reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only describes standard tensile testing, DIC, and EBSD methods on different alloys (FeCoNiAlTiMo and an unspecified alloy); neither passage provides any data or discussion on solute drag, dislocation dynamics, or mechanical behavior of WTaTiVZr or pure W. The key premises about solute drag, dynamic recovery, and their link to plasticity and toughness are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Refractory solutes (Ta, Ti, V, Zr) in W generate a solute drag effect on dislocations.
Solute drag delays dislocation pile-up and promotes dynamic recovery.
Solute drag leads to smoother, more homogeneous plastic deformation and enhanced toughness.
These effects are predominantly intragranular rather than grain-boundary-mediated.
The proposed mechanisms operate at ~1000 °C under inert atmosphere.
